title: Prediction of heat transport across solid interfaces in devices

concept.text: Discovered Materials grand challenge 05: understand and predict heat transport across solid interfaces in devices, to enable energy-efficient computing. Sources given: https://discoveredmaterials.com/grand-challenges/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to MAS on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: Grand challenge published by Discovered Materials (Matforge Inc.), open as of November 2026 with a USD 1 million prize pool; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Prediction of thermal boundary conductance
page.definition: A model predicts thermal boundary conductance—the heat flux divided by the temperature drop across a solid–solid interface—from temperature and specified interface structure, without fitting a conductance separately to each specimen.

goal.need: In three gold/polymer/silicon stack series, adhesion layers changed the fitted combined boundary conductance while retaining the polymer and substrate. Below 10 nm polymer thickness, the measured response departed from the prediction using bulk polymer conductivity alone. These measurements show why device heat-flow calculations require interface properties as well as bulk conductivity.

figures.caption: Boundary conductance in three stack series reported on 2 April 2020
figures.note: PMMA is poly(methyl methacrylate). Values combine the boundaries on both sides of PMMA, including the native silicon oxide contribution. Reported total experimental uncertainty: 10%.

statements.quote: This research thrust is to develop theoretical methods that are able to characterize phonon properties of a non-periodic system
statements.context: The nanoscale thermal-management thrust requires these methods to include heterogeneous materials, interfaces and defects without fitting parameters. Phonons are quantized lattice vibrations.

completion.title: Discovered Materials accepts a model that passes its public and hidden interface-conductance tests.
completion.criterion: The sponsor determines that one computational framework meets every Problem 05 criterion: reproducing all three public benchmark datasets, then predicting hidden solid–solid interfaces with the model frozen. Predictions must improve on the acoustic and diffuse mismatch models without degrading cases those models already describe correctly, and agree with atomistic reference calculations where available. Code must reproduce the results, and conductance must not be fitted separately to each specimen.
completion.set_by: Discovered Materials (Matforge, Inc.), Problem 05 and Official Rules, Sections 4–5; rules updated on 5 November 2026.
completion.threshold_quote: A challenge is "solved" only when a submission meets every success criterion in its Challenge Description, as determined by Sponsor under Section 5.
completion.basis: This prize tests the stated capability directly. The three parallel milestones below form its public validation set; the next step freezes the model for hidden-interface evaluation. Acceptance therefore requires transfer beyond reproducing known measurements. Problem 05 is listed as open.

milestones.title: A model reproduces Al/Si and Al/GaN thermal boundary conductance over 80–700 K.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce both temperature curves for sharp Al(111)/Si(111) and Al(111)/GaN(0001), including 379 and 423 MW m⁻² K⁻¹ at 300 K, respectively, and the renewed approximately linear increase above 400 K. Li et al., published on 20 August 2022, measured these two benchmark interfaces by time-domain thermoreflectance, which infers heat transport from the optical response to pulsed heating.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Problem 05, temperature-dependence benchmark for two metal/semiconductor interfaces.
milestones.threshold_quote: Reproduce the measured G(T) curves for Al(111)/Si(111) and Al(111)/GaN(0001) over 80–700 K

milestones.title: A model reproduces the 48% conductance increase from a 10 nm TiC layer between copper and diamond.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce the sponsor’s selected comparison from Chang et al. (2019): G(Cu/TiC/diamond)/G(Cu/diamond) = 1.48 for a highly crystalline 10 nm titanium-carbide interlayer, relative to that study’s direct copper/diamond reference.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Problem 05, carbide-interlayer benchmark for copper/diamond.

milestones.title: A model reproduces the thickness response of three gold/polymer/silicon stacks.
milestones.criterion: Reproduce the PMMA-thickness response of Au/PMMA/Si, Au/Ti/PMMA/Si and Au/Ni/PMMA/Si in Sandell et al., published on 2 April 2020, with nominally 2 nm adhesion layers, including the combined boundary terms tabulated above. Figures 4–5 and Table 2 define the targets. The three stack series were measured at three positions per specimen, with three acquisitions per position; the reported 10% experimental uncertainty is not a published model-acceptance tolerance.
milestones.set_by: Discovered Materials, Problem 05, bonding-layer benchmark for inorganic/polymer stacks.
milestones.threshold_quote: Reproduce the measured dependence on PMMA thickness

not_found: The challenge documents give no numerical prediction-error tolerance, runtime ceiling, hidden-test sample count or complete hidden-interface list.
No published demonstration or sponsor announcement of one model passing the public and hidden tests was found.
Chang et al.’s publisher full text could not be opened; the copper/diamond target is documented on the sponsor’s challenge page.
Independent specimen counts for the benchmark datasets were not established.
